In 2022, developed countries mobilized $115.9 billion for climate finance, but the efficiency of these investments is declining. Private co-financing per public dollar fell to just 24 cents, down from 51 cents in 2013. 

How can we make every dollar work smarter to catalyze systemic change? 

On the first day of the 15th IRENA Assembly, it was a pleasure to speak at the Ministerial Roundtable on Scaling Up Finance to Support the Energy Transition in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies. 

To address the financing gap, we must act decisively: 

1- Lower the cost of capital for clean energy in EMDEs through de-risking mechanisms, blended finance, and performance-based instruments. 

2- Streamline international support by creating strategic alliances and deepening collaboration for bankable projects, unlocking a $65 billion investment opportunity to connect 265 million people to clean energy. 

3- Leverage tryptic of digital data and AI to optimize investment decisions, accelerating renewable projects and ensuring equitable energy access for local communities. 

Together, through smarter and more impactful investments, we can bridge the financing gap and drive an inclusive, sustainable energy transformation.
